summary: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, requires early detection to preserve vision. Current diagnostic techniques lack sensitivity to minute structural changes in the posterior eye, and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) may only detect damage after it has occurred. This project proposes the development of a polarization-sensitive swept source OCT (PS-SSOCT) system to map the birefringent properties of the posterior eye in a non-human primate model, enabling 3D imaging and minute changes to tissue stress.
